CALLER IS REPORTING A SPILL OF GASOLINE AT A GAS STATION THAT HAPPENED ON THE 28 DEC 2007. DURING THE TRAINING OF AN EMPLOYEE THERE WAS AN ACCIDENTAL DISCHARGE OF 2,000 DOLLARS WORTH OF GASOLINE INTO THE PARKING LOT AND ROADWAY. THE OWNER REFUSED TO REPORT THIS INCIDENT AND MADE HIS EMPLOYEES CLEAN THE SPILL BY POWER WASHING THE GASOLINE DOWN STORM DRAINS. THE OWNER HAS THREATENED THE EMPLOYEES SAYING THAT ONE OF THEM OWED HIM MONEY AND THAT IF HE TOLD ANYONE THAT HE WOULD "WHIP HIS BUTT" AND IT WOULD BE ON THE EMPLOYEE NOT HIM. THE OWNER HAS ALSO STATED THAT HE WOULD PAY EACH OF HIS EMPLOYEES 100 DOLLARS TO LIE ABOUT THE INCIDENT.

Medium Affected: AIR

Skytruth Analysis
CALLER REPORTS THAT A POLICE OFFICER HAD STOPPED AT THE GAS STATION NEXT TO THE ARCTIC ICE CO AND SMELLED AMMONIA. HE CALLED THE FD TO HAVE THEM INVESTIGATE. UPON ARRIVAL THEY FOUND THE PRESSURE RELIEF VALVE GOING OFF. THE FACILITY HAS 2-1000 LB VESSELS OF ANHYDROUS AMMONIA. THEY CLOSED THE STREETS AND THE BP STATION NEXT DOOR AND ATLANTA HAZ MAT TEAM CAME IN FOR ASSISTANCE. THERE WAS A FAILURE IN THE POP OFF VALVE AND THEY LOST APPROXIMATELY 1000 LBS OF AMMONIA WAS RELEASED DURING THE INCIDENT. THEY KEPT THE BUSINESS CLOSED UNTIL MORNING AND THEY HAD A CREW COME IN AND REPAIR THE SYSTEM. THERE WERE NO INJURIES.

Report Description/// 10MAY24 48-HOUR PHMSA UPDATE TO NRC REPORT NUMBER 1398534 /// ON THURSDAY MAY 09 WILLIAMS CALLED THE NRC TO REPORT AN INCIDENT ON LINE2443 IN THE NW PIPELINE SYSTEM NEAR MILEPOST 112.5 IN WOLF CREEK, OREGON. THE INCIDENT OCCURRED DURING THE REMOVAL OF COATING ON THE PIPELINE WHILE COMPLETING AN EXPLORATORY DIG BASED ON AN ILI RUN. CAUSE OF THE LEAK IS CURRENTLY UNDER INVESTIGATION AND MORE INFORMATION WILL BE PROVIDED IN THE 30 DAY REPORT INCLUDING ESTIMATED LEAK VOLUME. THE LEAK WAS TEMPORARILY REMEDIATED WITH A PLIDCO LEAK CLAMP. THERE IS A PRESSURE REDUCTION ON THE LINE SINCE THE ONSET OF THE DIG CONSIDERED REPORTABLE DUE TO AN APPROXIMATE COST TO REPAIR OF $200,000. PERMANENT REPAIR BY CUTOUT IS EXPECTED TO BE COMPLETED 15JUN24. ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION OF INCIDENT: NATURAL GAS RELEASED FROM A 10 INCH PIPELINE THAT WAS FOUND DURING EXCAVATION WHEN THEY LOCATED AN ANOMALY.

SOMETIME IN THE EARLY MORNING A VESSEL SECURED IN VENTURA HARBOR SUDDENLY TOOK ON WATER AND SANK. THE HARBOR PATROL WAS ALERTED AT 6 AM AND RESPONDED TO FIND A 32' BAYLINER MOTOR VESSEL SUBMERGED IN THE SLIP. INSPECTION OF THE AREA REVEALED LIGHT PETROLEUM PRODUCT IN THE WATER IN THE VICINITY OF THE SUNKEN BOAT. HARBOR PATROL PUT OUT BOOM TO CATCH ANY ADDITIONAL PETROLEUM PRODUCT THAT MAY EXIT THE VESSEL. INTERVIEW OF THE OWNER REVEALED HE WAS IN THE PROCESS OF SELLING THE VESSEL AND HAD REMOVED ALL THE FUEL FROM THE TANK EITHER THE DAY BEFORE OR TWO DAYS EARLIER. THE PETROLEUM PRODUCT IN THE WATER WAS POSSIBLY OIL FROM THE ENGINE OR BILGE AREA.

Location2: QUIK TRIP GAS STATION

Material: FORMIC ACID
Medium Affected: AIR
Suspected Responsible Party: ATOTECH
SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 34.912855, -80.978203 (Approximated from premise)
Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTS AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF FORMIC ACID WAS RELEASED TO THE AIR, THE BACK OF THEIR VAN, AND STRAPS. THE MATERIAL CAME FROM BLUE 1-2 GALLON CONTAINERS. THE CAUSE OF THE RELEASE IS UNKNOWN TO CALLER, THEY BELIEVE THE MATERIAL MAY HAVE BEEN IMPROPERLY PACKAGED. THE INCIDENT OCCURRED WHILE THE VEHICLE WAS IN MOTION. CALLER STATES THEY DROVE 8 MINUTES TO THE GAS STATION. THEY THEN CONTACTED THEIR DISPATCHER AT 1613 INFORMING THEM THAT THEY WERE BEING IMPACTED THE MATERIAL RELEASED. THEY HAD ITCHY EYES, RUNNY NOSE, A HEADACHE, AND THEIR THROAT HURT. DURING THIS TIME CALLER STATES THEY WERE TOLD THE MATERIAL THEY WERE CARRYING WAS NOT A HARMFUL CHEMICAL. ONCE THE MATERIAL WAS TAKEN BACK TO THE FACILITY THEY WERE INFORMED BY THEIR DISPATCHER THAT THE MATERIAL WAS IN FACT A HARMFUL CHEMICAL. CALLER STATES THEIR VAN HAD BEEN LOADED WITH 2,200 POUNDS OF FORMIC ACID. THE MATERIAL WAS IN SMALL 1-2 GALLON CONTAINERS. IT WAS SUPPOSED TO GO TO SANTA ANA, CALIFORNIA. CALLER STATES THEY HAVE IMAGES AVAILABLE UPON REQUEST.

WHILE WALKING ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER’S BANK (ALONG THE REVETMENT) ON DECEMBER 17, 2010, SMALL SHEEN CIRCLES WERE OBSERVED ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRED ON NOVEMBER 10, 2010, AND WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC UNDER INCIDENT REPORT # 959615 AND LDEQ SPOC SYSTEM INCIDENT REPORT # GT01 8451. THIS AREA IS CURRENTLY BEING INVESTIGATED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE LDEQ (AI NO. 1708) WITH THE LDEQ.

Report Description///THIS IS AN UPDATE TO 1403144/// THE UPDATED INFORMATION IS AS FOLLOWS: THE RAILROAD HAS BEEN UPDATED TO ILLINOIS CENTRAL RAILROAD FROM WISCONSIN CENTRAL RAILROAD. THE CALLER REPORTED THAT NO LIQUID MATERIALS RELEASED FROM ANY OF THE CARS. (12) CUBIC YARDS OF NON-HAZARDOUS POLYETHYLENE PELLETS RELEASED FROM (1) CAR ONTO SOIL AND DETAILS OF THAT CAR HAVE BEEN UPDATED. THE RELEASED MATERIALS DID NOT RELEASE INTO ANY WATERWAYS AND MEDIUM IMPACTED HAS BEEN UPDATED. THE EVACUATION PREVIOUSLY IN PLACE HAS ENDED, TOTAL NUMBER OF EVACUATED IS STILL UNKNOWN. NO GRADE CROSSING INCIDENT OCCURRED. ORIGINALLY REPORTED INFO IS AS FOLLOWS: THE CALLER STATED THAT A FREIGHT TRAIN HAD (20) CARS THAT DERAILED DUE TO UNKNOWN CAUSES. BECAUSE OF THIS THERE IS A POTENTIAL FOR AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF AN UNKNOWN MATERIAL THAT COULD RELEASE. SHOULD MATERIAL RELEASE IT WOULD GO ONTO THE GROUND AND INTO AN UNKNOWN WATERWAY AT THE LOCATION. AN UNKNOWN TRACK WAS CLOSED IN ALL DIRECTIONS. THE PRICE POINT FOR DAMAGES HAS YET TO BE SET. ACCORDING TO THE CALLER A QUARTER MILE RADIUS AROUND THE INCIDENT LOCATION WAS EVACUATED, HOWEVER THE EXACT NUMBER OF EVACUEES IS UNKNOWN AT THIS TIME.
